summary: libcurl handles gss_unwrap GSS_S_BAD_SIG error incorrectly, allowing FTP response injection and heap memory leak.

claims.text: krb5_decode function does not handle GSS_S_BAD_SIG error properly and returns -1 without clearing buffer
claims.reasoning: The code confirms krb5_decode returns -1 on any gss_unwrap error (including GSS_S_BAD_SIG) and only prefixes the buffer with "599 " rather than clearing it entirely.

citations.note: krb5_decode checks if(maj != GSS_S_COMPLETE) at line 143, which catches GSS_S_BAD_SIG among other errors
Only clears first 4 bytes with strcpy(buf, "599 ") when len >= 4 at line 144-145
Returns -1 at line 146 without fully clearing the buffer

claims.text: defective krb5_decode function in libcurl FTP code
claims.reasoning: The function exists in the FTP/Kerberos code at the cited location.

citations.note: krb5_decode function defined at lines 128-154 in lib/krb5.c

claims.text: gss_unwrap returns GSS_S_BAD_SIG causing -1 return from krb5_decode
claims.reasoning: gss_unwrap returning GSS_S_BAD_SIG (or any non-GSS_S_COMPLETE status) triggers the error path that returns -1.

citations.note: gss_unwrap called at line 142, return value stored in maj
Check at line 143: if(maj != GSS_S_COMPLETE) catches GSS_S_BAD_SIG
Returns -1 at line 146 when gss_unwrap fails

claims.text: arbitrary FTP server responses can be injected and heap memory may be consumed as response
claims.reasoning: When krb5_decode returns -1, it becomes SIZE_MAX when assigned to size_t buf->size. buffer_read then reads far past the allocated buffer. The "599 " prefix could be interpreted as an FTP response, allowing injection.

citations.note: read_data assigns decode return value (int) to buf->size (size_t) at line 525-526
buffer_read uses buf->size without validation at line 534-536
Buffer prefixed with "599 " which is a valid FTP response code

claims.text: attacker sends crafted FTP data that triggers GSS_S_BAD_SIG error and causes -1 size handling
claims.reasoning: Attacker controls FTP server data stream. Malformed GSSAPI token triggers gss_unwrap -> GSS_S_BAD_SIG -> -1 return -> size_t overflow.

citations.note: socket_read reads encrypted data at line 522

claims.text: heap buffer read may leak confidential information via unallocated memory consumption
claims.reasoning: With buf->size = SIZE_MAX (from -1 conversion), buffer_read reads arbitrary heap memory past the buffer end, potentially leaking secrets via FTP responses or error messages.

citations.note: buffer_read computes len = buf->size - buf->index at line 534-535
memcpy reads from buf->data + buf->index at line 536
buf->size becomes SIZE_MAX when decode returns -1 at line 525-526

key_reasons: krb5_decode returns -1 on gss_unwrap failure (including GSS_S_BAD_SIG) without fully clearing buffer
read_data assigns signed int return to unsigned size_t buf->size causing integer overflow to SIZE_MAX
buffer_read uses unvalidated buf->size leading to heap overflow read
Attack path: malicious FTP server -> malformed GSS token -> gss_unwrap error -> -1 -> size_t overflow -> heap read -> data leak/injection
All cited functions and code paths exist at the checked revision
reply: Thank you for the detailed report. The code confirms the flaw: krb5_decode returns -1 on gss_unwrap failure (line 146), read_data assigns this to size_t buf->size causing overflow (line 525-526), and buffer_read reads past the buffer end (line 534-536). This allows heap memory disclosure and potential FTP response injection via the "599 " prefix. We will address this.
